headline: High-risk default data leakage and capability conflict: Langflow’s server-side filesystem/network access can feed next-ai-draw-io’s MCP/API-driven document processing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write/read server files and chain multiple agents; next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and natural-language commands. If Langflow outputs are placed into shared files or MCP-fed prompts, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from the profiles, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Langflow writes untrusted content into a file that next-ai-draw-io later ingests
IF next-ai-draw-io routes MCP or natural-language input directly into tool calls without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every file passed between the tools
Require a human review step before next-ai-draw-io processes Langflow output
Restrict Langflow outputs to a dedicated folder with read-only handoff
Disable automatic tool execution on imported text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow has broad network egress and handles per-flow credentials plus uploaded files; next-ai-draw-io can send documents to multiple third-party model APIs and MCP. If both touch the same workspace or document set, sensitive flow inputs or PDFs can be exfiltrated by default through outbound API calls. The blast radius includes secrets and document contents.
conditions: IF Langflow and next-ai-draw-io share a workspace or uploaded document store
IF next-ai-draw-io sends those documents to any configured external model API
IF Langflow flow inputs include secrets or intermediate outputs
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto different workspaces
Remove external model endpoints from next-ai-draw-io for sensitive runs
Store Langflow secrets outside any shared folder
Turn off network egress for one agent during document processing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can execute shell commands, install packages, write the filesystem, and run unsandboxed Python by default; next-ai-draw-io can use browsers, MCP, and broad network egress. If both operate on the same files or mutable project state, concurrent writes and side effects can collide and corrupt outputs. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or project files
IF Langflow Python components or shell steps modify artifacts while next-ai-draw-io is processing them
IF no external locking or orchestration isolation is configured
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable Langflow shell/package actions for shared runs
Pause next-ai-draw-io while Langflow mutates files
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and produce intermediate outputs; next-ai-draw-io is a document-processing assistant that can act on natural-language commands. If next-ai-draw-io treats Langflow output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. The pairwise pathway exists, but the blast radius is mainly work-product corruption.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes Langflow-generated text without verification
IF Langflow outputs are used as source material for diagram generation or edits
mitigations: Require a verification step before diagram generation
Mark Langflow output as untrusted in the UI
Compare generated diagrams against source documents
Limit automatic follow-on actions to preview mode
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and handles uploaded files on a server filesystem; next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, images, and text and can send them to external model providers. If regulated documents or secrets are routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are uploaded into either agent
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use a third-party API provider
IF Langflow retention exceeds the organization’s document-retention policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared runs
Use only local models in next-ai-draw-io for sensitive documents
Purge Langflow uploads after each run
Document retention settings for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems
